review: Independent static + fault-injection review of NFC backend

findings.evidence: Fault injection dropped first original TLV after SET. VERIFY_ADD detects mismatch, but STOP later reports routes cleaned / cleanflag1 with only5 original bytes remaining instead of10.
findings.requested: Retain original baseline and avoid false-clean status after ambiguous/partial mutation; verify preserved originals or retain explicit recovery uncertainty.
findings.fix: Retains baseline and intended installed table. Cleanup verifies original TLV multiset; restores known partial result to baseline only when no unknown entries exist. Missing baseline plus unknown changes remains RECOVERY.

findings.evidence: Mock accepts stop asynchronously without changing state. Timeout releases hook and marks clean. Accepted stop later reaches state0; repeated STOP returns Stopped but RF remains disabled.
findings.requested: Track accepted/inflight stop until completion and compensating discovery restart are resolved; never declare clean solely because stop has not completed yet.
findings.fix: Accepted stop_pending survives timeout; repeated STOP reuses it without a second command. Hook remains until state0 and compensating discovery restart completes.

findings.evidence: Snapshot allows complete253-byte TLV in255-byte notification payload; backend SET payload capped252 supports max250-byte TLV. If oversized opaque TLV follows smaller entries, prior SET_MORE can already be sent before serialization fails.
findings.requested: Dry-run every SET chunk before first mutation, including full command total-length bound.
findings.fix: write_table dry-runs every chunk with actual 252-byte payload bound before first SET.

conditional_risks.evidence: RF_GET_ROUTING notifications lack a transaction ID. HAL observer collects matching notifications while local GET is pending. No lock excludes concurrent stock GET/SET or route mutation between snapshot and SET. Per-command callback resolves RSP ownership but cannot prove notification ownership.
conditional_risks.limit: No firmware runtime concurrency trace. This remains an experimental integration risk, not a reproduced device failure or assurance of destructive behavior.

conditional_risks.evidence: Host mocks exercise bounded parser/state transitions but not real interrupt/task scheduling, controller SET commit semantics, callback-slot timing, or NFC stack shutdown/reset. Module remains resident; no unloading is approved by this review.
conditional_risks.limit: No installation or runtime firmware API calls were performed.

positive_checks: Route table and APDU buffers have checked bounded lengths in reviewed helpers
HAL callback remains resident and stock traffic is forwarded by design
Native transport directions and byte order match Android implementation

passed: prototype/tests/nfc_probe_test.c (lifecycle, route preservation, partial SET commit/reject, corrupted successful SET, unknown concurrent mutation containment, oversized TLV preflight, delayed STOP, deferred command callback, stale RF session)
prototype/tests/route_table_test.c (bounded snapshots, malformed/truncated entries, opaque TLV preservation, multi-packet roundtrip, conflicts)
prototype/android/build/review/pending_stop_regression.c (independent repeated-STOP check: no second hardware STOP while accepted request remains pending; eventual completion restores RF discovery)
validation.scope: Deterministic host fault-injection and source review; runtime compatibility remains unproven.

command_response_correlation.result: Completion comes from queued NFA per-command callback; raw same-opcode RSP is insufficient. Accepted command_pending survives timeout and blocks cleanup until callback plus final GET NTF. Deferred callback/raw-RSP fault injection passes.
command_response_correlation.evidence_reported_by_backend_agent: Exact firmware nci queue carries queued BT_HDR callback; NXP RSP handler dispatches event oid|0x40 and full NCI packet.
